[PC][Late 90s] Violent physics based fighting/brawler game with medieval fantasy setting. Platform(s): PC only I thik. Estimated year of release: late 90s Graphics/art style: early 3D graphics. Dark fantasy aesthetics. Physics based melee combat system, kind of like Exanima or Half Sword except the tech wasn't there yet. You could control how the character moved their weapons rather than playing preetermined animations. Thre was a dismerment system, a character could be dismembered and keep fighting, you could even pick up your severed leg and bludgeon your rival to death while jumping on one foot. I believe the voice acting was suitably over the top. There was a sort of campaign mode where you are let loose on a large level to kill a bunch of mobs, but there was also a VS mode in which you could control any of the characters, including tiny goblins. One of the levels had a lava river, and I seem to remember you had to go down it with a raft.

[PC] [2008 - 2014] Trying to remember an Anime Art Style Third Person Shooter with high mobility/Customizable clothes/ Weapon upgrade system. There was quite a niche third person shooter, where the characters clothes were customizable, you can buy weapons and upgraded them, and the art style was quite anime/asian. The gameplay was frenetic because you could dash almost every time to the sides, the maps were uniquely adapted to the mobility, quite made me remember something similar to the game **""""""""Gunz The Duel""""""""** type of mobility, but with anime style. There was a special game mode where someone becomes the death, I think only 1 per round, and they needed to kill everyone in a limited time. If you were the killer, you get a target to chase after, and if you kill him, you get double points, while if you kill anyone on sight, you just get one. The others could shoot him or use melee weapons, but they are not that effective because the killer was tanky as hell. So, you either most of the time use melee to hit him, and you would get him a little knock back and waste his time, or use the extremely fast and unique mobility of the game to run from him. I remember that everyone got a small HUD in the middle upside, in that mode where it shows how many people were left, how many of the killed were specific targets (green 2x points) or random (gray 1x points) and also the time remaining. I'm pretty sure the game shut down many years ago, but it was quite fun.
